references.text: Lists Jacob's twelve sons, corresponding to the list of those who went down to Egypt
Repeats the names of Israel's sons who came to Egypt, directly parallel to Genesis 46:8
Stephen refers to how Jacob and his entire family, 75 in total, went down to Egypt
Lists the sons of Israel (Jacob), with Reuben mentioned first as the firstborn
Reuben, Israel's firstborn, and his sons are mentioned in the census
This is the direct continuation of the same list and event that begins in Genesis 46:8.
Confirms and elaborates on Reuben's status as the firstborn in a later genealogical record.
A parallel genealogical list confirming Reuben's status and lineage in Exodus.
Establishes the same order of tribes and confirms Reuben's place as the firstborn in Chronicles.
Repeats the specific identification of Reuben as the firstborn and his sons in Chronicles.
Completes the historical account of the migration to Egypt by summarizing the number and status of Jacob's household.
New Testament confirmation of Jacob's sons (including Reuben and his brothers) as the foundation for God's history of salvation.
Explains the theological context behind Reuben's title as firstborn by mentioning the loss of rights.
Provides the reason for Reuben's loss of the birthright, adding depth to his title during the migration.
Confirms Reuben's status as the firstborn in an earlier phase of Jacob's life, before the migration to Egypt.
